title: NEON small mammal box trapping, RELEASE-2026: nightly capture counts of 143 species on 332 trapping grids at 46 NEON sites, 2013-2024
creator: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network)
citation: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network). Small mammal box trapping (DP1.10072.001), RELEASE-2026. https://doi.org/10.48443/a83h-tb34. Dataset accessed from https://data.neonscience.org/data-products/DP1.10072.001/RELEASE-2026 on 2026-11-02

intellectualRights.note: Licence stated on https://data.neonscience.org/data-api/ (NEON data products are CC BY 4.0); attribution per NEON's citation guidance

abstract: NEON samples small mammals (nonvolant, nocturnal, 5-500 g) on 10 x 10 grids of Sherman box traps at 10 m spacing, three to eight grids per terrestrial site, in bouts of one night (diversity grids) or three consecutive nights (pathogen grids) timed to the new moon, four to six bouts a year. This table is one row per trapping grid x bout x night x species for the 143 species-rank taxa, y = number of captures of the species on the grid that night, obs_traps_set = traps set, with every species carried as a zero on every surveyed grid-night (national pool; the sites where each species was captured are listed in __taxa). Built from the RELEASE-2026 basic package through the NEON API: 17,704 grid-nights, 1,612 bouts, 169,307 captures.
samplingProtocol: Sherman box traps (LFA/XLK) on 10 x 10 grids at 10 m spacing, set in the evening and checked at dawn; bouts within 10 days of the new moon, 1 night (diversity grids) or 3 consecutive nights (pathogen grids); captured animals identified, ear-tagged (or PIT-tagged) and measured; NEON protocol NEON.DOC.000481
surveyEvidenceNote: mam_perplotnight: a grid-night is a survey iff samplingImpractical is NA or OK, gridCompletion is recorded, and at least one trap was set (mam_pertrapnight trapStatus other than '1 - trap not set'); impractical nights are deposited with 100 'trap not set' rows and are dropped. Species pool is national (E4 full rectangle): every species-rank taxon has a row at every surveyed grid-night, so a species outside its range at a site is a structural zero there; taxon_sites in __taxa lists the sites where each species was captured.
closure: period = trapping bout (eventID, 1-6 nights per grid, usually 1 or 3, within at most 12 days); occasion = night within the bout at the grid; population open between bouts (robust design)
geographicCoverage: 46 NEON terrestrial sites in the contiguous United States and Alaska (no Hawaii or Puerto Rico); plot centres latitude 17.97 to 71.25, longitude -156.50 to -66.83, as published by NEON

coordinatesCoarsened.method: As published by NEON: agency-published plot centres with coordinateUncertainty (the E7 agency exception). The Florida mouse Podomys floridanus (IUCN VU) is among the shipped taxa; NEON publishes these plot coordinates itself, and its own obfuscation of listed taxa (D01 state-listed species to higher rank, per the product issue log) is applied upstream

covariateNote: obs_grid_method is the grid's sampling method that bout (pathogen = 3 nights with blood/ear/hair samples, diversity = 1 night); grids changed method across years at some sites. unit_* are NEON's plot attributes; a few grids carry two published coordinates across the years (modal kept, n_published_coordinates in __units).
designNote: Repeated counts within closed bouts (N-mixture per bout) and an open population across bouts (robust-design counts). The companion table neon_2026_smallmammals_rd carries the individual capture histories (same __periods).

components.sibling: neon_2026_smallmammals_rd (same deposit, same bouts and __periods; individual robust-design histories)

notes: Species pool is national (see surveyEvidenceNote); a community model should restrict each site to the species that can occur there (taxon_sites in __taxa gives the sites with at least one capture) rather than read the out-of-range zeros as surveyed absences. taxon is NEON's four-letter taxonID. Captures identified above species rank are not shipped and their counts are not in y.
